interpretation: The original large Q21/Q33 slowdowns did not reproduce in this diagnostic. The primary losses remain recorded; this is not proof of a fix or of a specific external cause.

Q88 remains slower and variable. Disabling shuffle compression for both engines did not eliminate the regression. The separate default-compression control ran after the disabled cohort; changing host/JVM state and fixed cohort order limit causal attribution.

The combined TPC-DS JFR spans Q21/Q33/Q88. LZ4JavaSafeFastDecompressor appears in 5911/6712 native-named-worker and 4278/6399 stock-named-worker Java ExecutionSamples. These are inclusive Java-stack sample fractions, not percentages of whole-job CPU or proof that LZ4 causes the native/stock gap.

NativeMethodSample remains separate because it can include blocking. The OS native sample resolves Parquet push decoding, dictionary/RLE decoding and Arrow take code; it is not a complete Rust CPU profile.

Clustering JFR did not reproduce the prior Paimon2.0 loss. Java Parquet dictionary/equality work appears in stock/previous writer samples; native writer samples retain Java sorting/hash work. Sparse, unequal-duration samples do not establish component speedup or explain the earlier loss.
